newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says suspends contact with Bosnian embassy.
newsitem.headline: Germany says suspends contact with Bosnian embassy.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said in a statement on Sunday that Germany had suspended contact with Bosnia's embassy in Bonn.

"As from yesterday, there has been an official freezing of contacts," Kinkel said in a statement, adding the move followed a recommendation given on Saturday by the international community's High Representative in Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp.

Western allies had threatened to impose penalties on the joint postwar government of Bosnia unless it reached agreement on three key laws by Friday -- a deadline set by NATO at a summit in May in Sintra, Portugal.
But in making his recommendation, Westendorp said he had extended the deadline until Monday because on two of the laws, governing passports and citizenship, good progress had been made.
The German Foreign Ministry statement however cited only the Friday deadline in explaining its reasons for the move, adding that its patience had run out.

"Without any perceptible readiness by leaders in Bosnia to reach a self-supporting peace through joint efforts, all international efforts are being undermined. The international community cannot allow this," Kinkel said.
